title: Remaped keys CTRL+C/V to ALT+C/V insert @copiedString@ into PowerShell 7.1.4 console
author: siegfriedcw
summary: Remapped shortcuts can add at-signs in standalone PowerShell, ConEmu, and RDP while Windows Terminal is unaffected.

confidence.rationale: The symptom pattern is strong, but the malformed synthetic event is not identified.

judgment.rationale: The host split and event timing justify tracing injection, but no event trace proves the exact field.
evidence: A contributor reproduced it on PowerShell 7.1.4.
One at-sign appears on key press and another on modifier release.
It persists on 0.100.2 in ConEmu and RDP but not Windows Terminal.

fix_assessment.rationale: No concrete existing fix covers the reported path; the lightweight hypothesis is ready for a bounded design workflow.

actions.label: Trace remapped keys in legacy PowerShell

steps: Paste into standalone PowerShell or ConEmu.
Repeat in Windows Terminal as a control.
reproduce.expected_result: Pasted text contains no added at-signs.

proposed_fixes.title: Normalize synthetic events for legacy console hosts
proposed_fixes.root_cause: A generated modifier or key-up sequence is likely interpreted as @ by legacy console input translation.
plan: Capture the same remap's low-level events in ConsoleHost and Windows Terminal.
Correct ordering, scan-code, or Unicode flags only after isolating the translated event.
verification: Paste with Alt+V to Ctrl+V and confirm no added @ in either console host.

confidence.rationale: The symptom pattern is strong, but the malformed synthetic event is not identified.
